## Outcome

There was no major new public feature commit. I used the week to verify open branches before the final coding push.

## What I Did

- Checked that PR #336 preserved explicit `showSelected` in all tested variants.
- Checked that PR #339 measured and placed multiple strip lines after upstream changes.
- Checked that PR #288 assertions were independent of one output height.
- Checked that PR #253 covered both wide and tall viewports.
- Evaluated which final feature could be explored without misrepresenting unfinished work.
- Clarified PR #285’s error path: `facet_wrap(~Species)` works, while `. ~ Species` produces the confusing unsupported-notation behavior.

## Learnings

A quiet GitHub week can prevent a noisy final week. Verifying assumptions before opening another large branch led to a focused final proof of concept: recomputing `stat_bin` after selection.

## Challenges / Notes

Verification is easy to under-report because it produces fewer new commits. The useful outcome was knowing which behavior and test boundaries were ready for the final week.

## Next Week Targets

Build a failing `stat_bin + showSelected` acceptance test, then implement the smallest browser-side proof of concept that passes it.
